Its former {{ill|Shakaku|ja|社格|ko|사격 (신토)|zh|社格|qid=Q10444029}} was gōsha. It is one candidate shrine for Hieta Shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engishiki list}}. {{nihongo|'''Hieta Shrine'''|薭田神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Musashi Province]].

==Enshrined deities==
*{{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Q317997|qid=Q317997|qid=Q317997|lt=Hondawake-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Amaterasu|Q455602|qid=Q455602}}, {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|Q1073668|qid=Q1073668}} no Mikoto, Arakita no Sotsuhiko no Mikoto, {{ill|Kasuga-no-Kami|Q11088805|qid=Q11088805|lt=Kasuga Ōkami}}

==History==
According to shrine tradition, this shrine was founded in {{ill|709|Q23514|qid=Q23514}} ({{ill|Wadō (era)|Q1373026|qid=Q1373026}} 2) by {{ill|Gyōki|Q1136664|qid=Q1136664}}.

It is an old shrine also recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}. It was originally "'''Kamata Shrine'''," but since an old character form of "Kama" was used and repeatedly miswritten as "Hie," the reading eventually became "Hieta Jinja"<ref name="史跡散歩">Yoshiyuki Niikura, "Ōta-ku Historic Walk (Tokyo Historic Guide 11)," {{ill|Gakuseisha|Q11448819|qid=Q11448819}}, 1992, pp.79-80</ref>.
